dashboard_line: Bundle compression analysis complete: 8 critical findings, risk_score=62, FFMx payload compression viable

code_quality_signals: strong_architecture (0.85): modular, layered design; clear separation of concerns
maintainability_concern (0.61): NECTAR caching logic + bundle validation lacks inline documentation
correctness_gaps (0.74): three race conditions detected; atomic writes mitigate but edge cases remain

detailed_findings.issue: Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race on _nectar_cache_ts. Under W1 parallel load (4-5 agents spawning within 1ms), multiple agents can bypass TTL check and trigger redundant file reads.
detailed_findings.evidence: Line 353: cache TTL check uses `time.monotonic()` without synchronization lock; W1 parallel dispatch can cause cache invalidation storms
detailed_findings.impact: Potential 5-10 redundant NECTAR.md reads per W1 cycle; token budget wasted on duplicate context; unpredictable behavior under concurrent access
detailed_findings.remediation: Wrap _nectar_cache_ts update in asyncio.Lock; ensure TTL check + update are atomic

detailed_findings.issue: Silent truncation of HONEY.md at 5K token budget (20K chars) without changelog. Agents receive incomplete context; manifest_truthfulness may suffer if agents cannot access necessary principles.
detailed_findings.evidence: Line 325-326: truncates at 20K chars with placeholder message. No validation that truncation preserved critical sections (e.g., spawn discipline boilerplate)
detailed_findings.impact: HONEY.md integrity compromised; agent self-awareness degrades; downstream manifests show lower belief_index due to incomplete context
detailed_findings.remediation: Parse HONEY.md frontmatter + key sections before truncation; preserve mandatory sections (principles, discipline boilerplate); log what was dropped

detailed_findings.issue: Counter state is in-memory dict with no persistence. If ManifestWriter is recreated (e.g., process restart), collisions possible between old and new counter sequences within same second.
detailed_findings.evidence: Line 597: `self._counter_state = {}` has no lock-free read-modify-write semantics; counter is ephemeral
detailed_findings.impact: Collision risk for manifest filenames; breaks immutability guarantee (forensic principle violated); manifest recovery becomes ambiguous
detailed_findings.remediation: Initialize counter from filesystem state at startup; scan existing manifest files in target dir to bootstrap counter. OR: use UUID instead of counter for collision-free naming

detailed_findings.issue: Card trimming logic at line 377-379 is aggressive but fragile: keeps first 800 chars + last 200 chars. Risk of breaking YAML frontmatter or splitting mid-instruction.
detailed_findings.evidence: Line 375-379: splits card at character boundary without parsing structure. If card has frontmatter (YAML), boundary may slice through metadata
detailed_findings.impact: Agent cards receive corrupted or incomplete behavioral templates; agent type-to-official-type mapping may fail; spawn discipline boilerplate gets truncated
detailed_findings.remediation: Parse card frontmatter + body separately; truncate body only, preserve frontmatter + closing section intact

detailed_findings.issue: Wave parameters (max_parallel, timeout_seconds, model) are hardcoded at module level. No environment variable override, no per-investigation-label customization. Breaks equilibrium constraint: cannot tune system response without editing source.
detailed_findings.evidence: Lines 100-122: WAVE_PARAMS is a static dict. No Config class or env-var reader to allow runtime tuning
detailed_findings.impact: Cannot adapt wave parameters to different investigation contexts (e.g., W1 haiku may be too weak for deep synthesis; no way to upgrade to sonnet mid-investigation)
detailed_findings.remediation: Externalize WAVE_PARAMS to config file (JSON/YAML) or environment variables; add override capability at dispatch_wave() call site

detailed_findings.issue: Rate limiter has both async and sync methods, but sync_acquire() does not have asyncio.Lock guard. W1 parallel spawn with both async + sync contexts causes token bucket state corruption.
detailed_findings.evidence: Lines 777-789: acquire_sync() modifies self._tokens without lock; async path uses self._lock but sync path bypasses it
detailed_findings.impact: Rate limit enforcement becomes probabilistic; API quota may be exceeded during W1 LIFTOFF; cost overruns possible
detailed_findings.remediation: Unify to async-only (preferred) or use threading.Lock for true sync safety. Audit _is_async_context() usage pattern

detailed_findings.issue: Bundle validation only checks for marker strings, not semantic correctness. Missing: dashboard_line length check, compass_edge valid values (N/S/E/W), quality_score/belief_index bounds (0.0-1.0).
detailed_findings.evidence: Lines 476-487: only searches for marker presence; no schema validation
detailed_findings.impact: Invalid manifests can be written; downstream agents receiving corrupt bundles; scout/compass-navigator agents may fail to parse signals
detailed_findings.remediation: Add schema validator (JSON schema or Pydantic model); check bounds, format, semantic constraints before bundle is injected

detailed_findings.issue: COC entry subprocess failure (line 738-739) is caught and logged as warning only. No fallback or retry. Critical forensic signal lost silently.
detailed_findings.evidence: Lines 738-739: subprocess timeout/error → log.warning(), return; manifest written but COC entry missing
detailed_findings.impact: Forensic chain of custody broken; audit trail incomplete; cannot prove manifest was generated by legitimate agent (reputation scoring unreliable)
detailed_findings.remediation: Retry COC write with exponential backoff; if still failing, raise exception and fail the manifest write (transactional guarantee)

positive_findings.note: Excellent atomic write pattern: temp file + fsync + rename (POSIX atomic). Prevents partial-read corruption. This is correct.
Uses asyncio.TaskGroup (Python 3.11+) for structured concurrency. Proper exception handling via ExceptionGroup. Clean + correct.
Comprehensive 8-test self-test suite covers core workflows (bundle composition, manifest write, dry-run). Good validation practice.
Correct layering of context: global HONEY → project HONEY → NECTAR → pollen → card → task. Respects faerie2 principles.

compression_impact_assessment.findings_vs_ffmx: FFMx report claims 2.2× compression via dashboard-line limitation (30.8K tokens/manifest vs. 65K+ transcripts). Implementation_spec.py validates this: ManifestWriter outputs manifest JSON + dashboard_line (80-char capped). However, bundle composition (BundleComposer) can inflate context significantly due to HONEY/NECTAR/card inlining. NECTAR caching is critical to achieving 0.54× cost savings; race condition (FFMx-1) jeopardizes this.
compression_impact_assessment.risk_to_ffmx_metric: If NECTAR TTL race causes redundant reads or bundle validation fails (FFMx-7), actual measured compression may degrade to 0.65-0.75× instead of claimed 0.54×. This would lower FFMx from 44.4 to ~35-38, a 15-20% degradation.

recommendations: IMMEDIATE (before W1 production): Fix FFMx-1 (NECTAR TTL race) and FFMx-3 (manifest counter collision). Both affect forensic integrity.
HIGH PRIORITY: Implement FFMx-2 (HONEY truncation tracking) and FFMx-4 (card excerpt parsing). Both affect agent context completeness.
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Externalize WAVE_PARAMS (FFMx-5) and add bundle schema validation (FFMx-7). Both improve maintainability + flexibility.
CONSIDER: Unified async-only design (remove sync fallback) or true threading.Lock for rate limiter (FFMx-6).
next_steps: Implement atomic NECTAR cache with asyncio.Lock
Add manifests tests for counter collision scenarios
Create JSON schema for bundle validation
Spike: measure actual compression ratio in production (compare claimed vs. observed FFMx)
observed_patterns: Bundle composition respects faerie2 principles (good); async architecture is modern + correct
Caching strategy is sound (TTL + 5-min piston wave cadence match); race condition is implementation detail, not design flaw
Manifest naming (date-organized, task_id-in-filename) follows forensic standard correctly
Error handling is mostly graceful; COC entry failure is the weak spot
